question: Which canonical mappings preserve document meaning through Markdown parse/serialize, and where must loss be explicit?
trigger: The owner asked whether Plate v2 needs the table-cell list support that main gained in PR 5139 (issue 5138), then asked for this review. The owner named the scope; it is not the unit `next` returned.
requirements: Preserve representable Markdown meaning in GFM table cells; diagnose intentional or unsupported loss and obey lossPolicy.
A GFM row stays on one line: no cell content may write a raw newline into the row.

Read the Markdown Plate writes on main: since PR 5139, main writes indent-list paragraphs in a cell as inline
    /
      /
    1. HTML and cell line breaks as
      .
Keep Markdown parsing DOM-free and keep the selective registered-tag grammar; raw HTML outside a named form stays literal and diagnosed.
The format compiler owns intrinsic syntax; features own their mappings.
evidenceReuse: Reused the 2026-09-28 dialect decision and the design D6, D8 and D18 rows as law. Rechecked the table cell, row and table encoders, the runtime list writer and the raw-HTML decoder on the current tree, and ran headless probes against the built dist and the next test editor.
summary:
Pursue. On next, a table cell holding list paragraphs refuses, and the refusal cascades through the row and the table: under the default lossPolicy reject the whole serialize fails and copy writes no text/markdown, and under allow the whole table disappears. A line break inside a cell paragraph becomes a space with no diagnostic, and a trailing break writes a raw newline into the row, which corrupts the table on re-read. Main already writes cell lists as inline
    /
      HTML, which next reads as literal tag text. The strongest target lets the Markdown runtime represent indent-list paragraphs and breaks inside a phrasing-only container as one-line inline
        /
          /
        1. and
          HTML, read back by the table decoder, which already sees each cell's children whole. Reusing the feature HTML mappings loses, because their output is verbose, unsafe in a GFM row and not main's form, and reading it back needs a DOM that Markdown parsing avoids.

callSites.current: No public call changes. Today the table cell markdown.encode runs encode(children); a list paragraph group returns an mdast list, so the cell refuses with "Markdown table cells can only contain inline content", the row and the table refuse in turn, and serialize fails under reject or drops the table under allow. Breaks pass through as mdast break and GFM writes a space. On parse, <ul><li> in a cell reaches the D8 html decoder and stays literal text with one warning per tag.

alternatives: Keep refusing: loses as the target. It is honest about loss but fails every export of a document with a list in any cell, drops the whole table under allow, and cannot read main output.

Flatten list paragraphs into paragraphs joined by
with markdown-property-omitted warnings for listType and indent: viable fallback that keeps text and explicit loss, but it drops structure GFM viewers render from HTML and still cannot read main output.

Reuse the feature HTML mappings to write and read HTML in cells: Stop. The Markdown mapping contract exposes no HTML encode or decode, although every editor compiles the HTML artifact. HTML serialize runs headless and round-trips a cell's list paragraphs, but it writes one <ul>/<ol> per item with data-* attributes and margin styles, leaves | and raw newlines unescaped (each breaks the GFM row) and does not match main's form. HTML parse needs a DOM that Markdown parsing avoids and drops main's <input type="checkbox"> task markup. The 2026-09-28 design rejected routing raw HTML to the HTML owner for the DOM and pairing cost.
Register ul, ol and li as Plate tags: Stop. Dialect law demotes registered block tags inside a tableCell to literal text, and lists are Markdown-native outside cells.

Cell-scoped inline HTML list syntax owned by the Markdown runtime and used by the table cell and table mappings, the form PR 5139 ships on main: Pursue. Lossless for indent lists, rendered by GFM viewers, reads main output and stays DOM-free.
Narrow the refusal cascade so one unrepresentable cell keeps its column with a diagnostic instead of dropping the table under allow: candidate for the plan, independent of lists.
proofLimits: Source inspection plus headless probes against the platejs dist built on 2026-10-02 and the next test editor; the encoders and decoders traced did not change in later commits. No browser, clipboard, GitHub rendering check, package suite or Benchmark run. Reading main output is shown with a hand-written <ul><li> cell, not a corpus of main exports. The HTML-reuse rejection rests on headless HTML probes (serialize, linkedom parse and cell slicing) and source tracing, not a Markdown runtime prototype; calling the compiled HTML artifact from inside the Markdown runtime was not run. Evidence lives in gitignored docs/plans/artifacts and must be force-added when committed.
